title: FIFA president Infantino faces rapid erosion of support after private equity plan
dek: Gianni Infantino attempted to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms without notifying his organization, triggering mass defection from confederations and his closest allies. UEFA threatened a World Cup boycott, and multiple confederation leaders signaled this may be the best opportunity to remove him.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: UEFA threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, on Thursday in response to Infantino's private equity plan.
bottom_line: The scale and speed of confederation defection and internal resignations are documented facts; whether this moment proves fatal to Infantino's tenure or resolves into another cycle of FIFA crisis and institutional continuity remains unwritten. Watch for formal removal procedures initiated by confederations or a consolidated statement from the majority of FIFA's voting members in the coming weeks.
body: In less than 72 hours, FIFA president Gianni Infantino moved from what observers describe as an unassailable position to the center of an institutional crisis. According to BBC Sport, Infantino attempted to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms apparently without the knowledge of anyone else in the organization.

The decision triggered immediate and coordinated defection across FIFA's confederation structure. UEFA threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, on Thursday, per BBC reporting. CONCACAF called for a full review into FIFA's leadership in light of the plan. The Asian Football Confederation shunned Infantino, according to the same source.
Infantino's inner circle fractured as well. Senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned, as did chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, both described by BBC Sport as among his closest allies.

Infantino backtracked in the early hours of Saturday morning. UEFA followed with a statement saying it had lost confidence in him. According to BBC Sport's analysis, UEFA senses the opportunity to remove Infantino and observers assess this is likely to be the best chance it will ever get to unseat him. Infantino was elected FIFA president in 2016.

The source material does not specify the identities of the private equity firms involved, the terms of the proposed stakes sale, or the specific FIFA competitions targeted. The exact mechanism or procedural avenue by which Infantino could be removed is not detailed in available reporting. No statements from Infantino defending his actions or explaining the rationale for the private equity approach are included in the reporting reviewed.
